items.title: Rusty Dedrick interviewed by Monk Rowe, Ellenville, New York, June 23, 1998
items.q: But Ray was a wonderful guy and a great player, and he fronted the band when he could and had another drummer. He was a great guy to work for.

ctx.x: So you got into — well Ray McKinley.
Well that was after the war, and I thank Red Norvo for that. Willard Alexander was backing Ray McKinley in a band. Eddie Sauter was the musical director, really wrote the
charts and rehearsed the band and everything. But Ray was a wonderful guy and a great player, and he fronted the band when he could and had another drummer. He was a great guy to work for.
